Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.Environment: Warm temperatures (24–30°C), high humidity, rainfall and overhead irrigation promote disease development.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.Spread: Spread through infected seeds, transplants, rain splash, irrigation water, contaminated tools and human handling.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.Description: Bacterial Spot is a serious disease of bell pepper that attacks leaves, stems and fruits. Severe infections cause leaf drop, reduce photosynthesis and lower fruit quality and market value.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small water-soaked lesions appear on young leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Dark brown to black spots enlarge and may develop yellow halos.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves fall prematurely and fruits develop raised scabby lesions.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Symptoms usually appear within 5–10 days after infection.

Treatment: Use copper mixed with mancozeb for improved disease management.
Recommended_Actions: Apply preventive copper sprays during humid weather.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.Environment: Well-drained fertile soil, full sunlight (6–8 hours daily), balanced fertilization and consistent irrigation.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.Description: The uploaded bell pepper leaf shows no visible signs of disease, pest infestation or nutrient deficiency. The plant appears healthy and capable of producing high-quality fruits.

Age_Cycle.Early: Healthy leaf emergence with uniform green coloration.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Continuous healthy growth throughout the growing season.

Organic_Treatment: Apply balanced organic fertilizers when necessary.
